clue.text: The exhilarating air of great French port

definitions.text: The exhilarating air of great French port

parts.words: The exhilarating air of great French port
parts.note: the stirring tune named after France's great Mediterranean port, which became the national anthem

explanation.surface: Someone breathes in the bracing sea air of a big French harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' looks like the breeze off the sea, but it is a tune: France's rousing national anthem takes its name from the port of Marseille.
explanation.definitionFit: The French national anthem is a stirring song named after the volunteers from Marseille who sang it.

clue.text: Fast work for painter?

parts.note: a painter is the rope at a boat's bow, and its job is to make the vessel fast to a quay

explanation.surface: An artist dashes off a quick canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: The painter is not an artist but the rope tied to a boat's bow; 'fast' means secured, not quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Tying a boat securely to a buoy or quay with ropes is what that rope is for.

clue.text: Seeing nothing in the duty list he finds a restful perch

indicators.note: the zero is placed inside the word for the list of duties

parts.note: a roster is a list of who is on duty when
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone scanning the duty rota sees no shift for them and settles down to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel is the male farmyard bird that roosts on a perch at night.

clue.text: An advocate of far-fetched actions

parts.note: someone who argues for measures that go to the far edge, beyond what moderates accept

explanation.surface: A lawyer pleads cases that strain belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far-fetched' suggests implausible, but here it means fetched from far out: actions at the political edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanatic or radical champions drastic measures well beyond the moderate centre.

clue.text: Cyril becomes averse to music

indicators.note: the name changes into a new word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Cyril turns against music.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'averse' as 'a verse': the words written to be sung, made by rearranging the letters of CYRIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Song words are a verse set to music, the text a composer sets.

clue.text: Acts as a receiver for the present

definitions.text: Acts as a receiver for the present

parts.words: Acts as a receiver for the present
parts.note: taking a gift, or taking something on for now, as a recipient does

explanation.surface: Someone stands in as official receiver for the time being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the present' looks like 'for now', but it is the gift being received; a receiver of stolen goods is a further false lead.
explanation.definitionFit: To take what is offered, such as a gift, is to be its recipient.

clue.text: The staying power of a leading minister when badly sat upon

indicators.note: the letters are put together badly, so they are mixed into a new order

parts.note: Min. is the short form of minister, as in a government title

explanation.surface: A senior minister shows endurance while being sat on hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges MIN (the leading three letters of minister, also its abbreviation) and SAT into STAMIN, with A at the end; 'upon' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance, the ability to keep going over a long effort, is staying power.

clue.text: After getting soaked the punter might put his shirt on it

definitions.text: After getting soaked the punter might put his shirt on it

parts.words: After getting soaked the punter might put his shirt on it
parts.note: a wet shirt is hung on a drying frame, and a gambler bets everything on a runner

explanation.surface: A gambler who has lost heavily bets all he has on a racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put his shirt on' is a betting idiom for staking everything on a horse; here the shirt, soaked in the wash, is literally hung on a wooden drying frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden frame for drying laundry is called a horse, one meant for clothes.

clue.text: A cave-man kept posted

parts.note: cave is schoolboy Latin for 'beware', shouted by the boy keeping watch, posted at his station

explanation.surface: A prehistoric man is kept up to date with the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave' is Latin for 'beware!', the warning cry of a British schoolboy keeping watch; that man is posted on guard, not sent letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry stationed to watch and warn is the man on watch.

clue.text: Chair carved, by the way, for three English kings

indicators.note: the chair is carved, so its letters are cut into a new shape

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A carved chair stands by the road, fit for three English monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carved' rearranges CHAIR into RICHA; 'by' just sets RD beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: England has had three monarchs of this name, among them the Lionheart and the one killed at Bosworth.

clue.text: It has overtaken the iron horse with powerful spurts in training

definitions.text: It has overtaken the iron horse with powerful spurts in training

parts.words: It has overtaken the iron horse with powerful spurts in training
parts.note: the iron horse is the steam locomotive, replaced by a motor that drives trains

explanation.surface: A racehorse in training puts on bursts of speed to pass a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron horse' is old slang for the steam locomotive; 'in training' means in trains, not in preparation for a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil-fuelled motors replaced steam in railway locomotives, firing by compression.

clue.text: How the list is growing despite scratchings

definitions.text: How the list is growing despite scratchings

indicators.note: horses scratched from a race reorder the runners' list, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of runners keeps getting longer even as horses are withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratchings' are withdrawals from a race, which reshuffle the list; THE LIST rearranges to a plant that keeps growing however it scratches.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickly weed scratches anyone who touches it yet flourishes regardless.

clue.text: Jack's turnover?

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and his turnover is his boat going upside down

explanation.surface: A small trader named Jack reports his sales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' looks like business takings, and Jack like a name; Jack is a sailor and the turnover is his boat rolling over.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat overturning in the water is the sailor's kind of turnover.

clue.text: He noted regal variations

indicators.note: variations of a word are its letters reworked, which also hints at a famous musical work

explanation.surface: A composer wrote variations on a stately royal theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variations' rearranges REGAL; it also points to the Enigma Variations. 'He noted' is a man who wrote notes, a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: The English composer of the Enigma Variations wrote music, putting down notes.

clue.text: Wasn't willing to pass anything on, apparently

definitions.text: Wasn't willing to pass anything on, apparently

parts.words: Wasn't willing to pass anything on, apparently
parts.note: someone who left no will died without willing their property to heirs

explanation.surface: A miser refused to hand anything down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' looks like 'keen'; it means making a will to leave property.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying with no valid will means the estate was not formally bequeathed.

clue.text: Swept up between Banks but treated Women's Institute badly

indicators.note: something treated badly is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: WI is the abbreviation for the Women's Institute, a British women's community organisation

explanation.surface: Someone named Banks mistreated the local Women's Institute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' looks like a surname; it is river banks. 'Badly' rearranges TREATED and WI.
explanation.definitionFit: Water carried up an estuary by the incoming sea, between its shores, is pushed by the tide.

clue.text: Indecisively erred

parts.note: erred read as 'said er', the noise of someone unsure what to say

explanation.surface: Someone made a mistake through lack of resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erred' looks like 'made a mistake', but it means 'said er', the sound of someone faltering.
explanation.definitionFit: Pausing in doubt, saying 'er', is what a wavering person does.

clue.text: Not thinking much of the others

definitions.text: Not thinking much of the others

parts.words: Not thinking much of the others
parts.note: having little regard for other people's needs, not low esteem for them

explanation.surface: Someone has a poor opinion of everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not thinking much of' usually means disdain; here it means giving others little thought at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A person concerned only with their own interests gives no thought to other people.

clue.text: Scot in charge on a beachhead in empty state, seeks some fare

definitions.text: in empty state, seeks some fare

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, as in 'scot-free'
the head of beach is its first letter, B

explanation.surface: A Scottish officer leads an assault on a beach in a desolate country and looks for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scot' looks like a Scotsman but is the old word for a levy, as in 'scot-free'. A hire car with no passengers is empty and looks for a fare.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired car with its light on, carrying no passenger, cruises looking for someone to pay to ride.

clue.text: Pinching? He'll take it in for you

definitions.text: Pinching? He'll take it in for you

parts.words: Pinching? He'll take it in for you
parts.note: pinching is stealing, and a receiver of stolen goods takes them in

explanation.surface: A tailor offers to take in clothes that pinch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinching' looks like tight clothes needing a tailor to take them in; it is slang for stealing, and the man who takes in the loot is a receiver.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal dealer who buys and sells on stolen goods is a receiver.

clue.text: If ten could be true they'd make a permanent establishment

indicators.note: the word could be something else, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Someone muses that if ten things were true they would build something lasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' rearranges IF, X and TRUE together; 'they'd make' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fixed in place for good, such as a built-in fitting, is permanent.

clue.text: How the nag kept saying "No"?

parts.note: the nag is a horse, and saying 'nay' sounds like a horse's cry

explanation.surface: A nagging person keeps refusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a scold but is an old horse; 'nay' (no) said over and over sounds like the horse's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's cry is a whinny, which sounds like someone saying 'nay'.

clue.text: Given vote, leader unwound

annotationWithheld.why: Given vote, leader unwound (7): RELAXED is X in an anagram of LEADER, but 'unwound' must be both the anagram signal and the definition, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Theological degree in 24 hours for father

indicators.note: the degree is placed inside the word for the period of time

parts.note: a day lasts 24 hours
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theology degree

explanation.surface: A father earns his divinity doctorate in a single day.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's informal word for its father, a parent.

clue.text: The bird who went all soft over Icarus?

definitions.text: The bird who went all soft over Icarus?

parts.words: The bird who went all soft over Icarus?
parts.note: Icarus flew on wings of wax that melted in the sun, so a bird named for waxen wings fits

explanation.surface: A bird falls in love with the mythical Icarus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went all soft over' looks like falling for someone; in the myth Icarus's wings were wax, which softened and melted near the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A crested songbird has red tips on its wings like drops of sealing wax.

clue.text: Clearly showed even C.I.D. could become confused

indicators.note: the letters are muddled into a new order

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch

explanation.surface: Even the detectives showed signs of being muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could become confused' rearranges EVEN and CID; 'could' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To demonstrate or reveal a feeling plainly is to display it.

clue.text: Get rougher as cuts become hard to swallow

definitions.text: Get rougher as cuts become hard to swallow

parts.words: Get rougher as cuts become hard to swallow
parts.note: meat cuts that grow chewy and hard to eat become harder, as spending cuts are hard to accept

explanation.surface: Austerity hardens as the spending cuts become unpalatable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts' and 'hard to swallow' suggest budget cuts that are unpopular; they are cuts of meat growing chewy.
explanation.definitionFit: To make or grow harder and more resistant is to harden.

clue.text: Will his next stage be as a son-in-law?

definitions.text: Will his next stage be as a son-in-law?

parts.words: Will his next stage be as a son-in-law?
parts.note: a young man courting a daughter may marry her and become her parents' son-in-law; stage also hints at a musical

explanation.surface: Parents wonder whether their daughter's suitor will marry her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' is a step in a courtship and also hints at a theatre musical, Sandy Wilson's 1950s show of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's young man, her sweetheart, may be the next son-in-law.
